alternatives.argument: The local Definition fully states the measurable input, label, and action spaces; source and target joint probability laws; input marginals; extended risks; supplied conditional label kernels; and exact covariate-shift hypotheses. The risk convention is independently supported by the complete fetch-verified Shalev-Shwartz and Ben-David textbook §§3.2.1–3.2.2 and complete fetch-verified Mansour et al. §§2–3. Kernel disintegration is stated as an explicit interface and proved by its direct supplier; no conditional-kernel existence is asserted.

The local Definition states d_{HDeltaH}=2 sup_{h,k}|muS(A_hk)-muT(A_hk)| and derives the range [0,2] from probability differences. The complete fetch-verified Mansour et al. Definition 3 supplies d_A(P,Q)=sup_{A in A}|P(A)-Q(A)| for A=HDeltaH; multiplying by two gives the displayed convention, while the local Definition states the disagreement sets and measurability. No proof depends on the unavailable endpoint.

For any h,g, the binary pointwise inequality 1{h(x) != y} <= 1{g(x) != y}+1{h(x) != g(x)} integrates under the target law to epsilonT(h) <= epsilonT(g)+muT(A_hg). The same inequality under the source law gives muS(A_hg) <= epsilonS(h)+epsilonS(g), while the divergence definition gives muT(A_hg) <= muS(A_hg)+d/2. Combining yields epsilonT(h) <= epsilonS(h)+epsilonS(g)+epsilonT(g)+d/2. For every eta>0, the definition of lambda as an infimum over a nonempty class supplies g_eta with epsilonS(g_eta)+epsilonT(g_eta)<lambda+eta. Substitute and let eta decrease to zero. This is the complete local proof in steps 1.1–2.2; it uses no attained minimizer, VC assumption, or choice axiom. Mansour et al. §3 is a complete independent treatment and is fetch-verified.
